title: What happened in AI — Jul 29, 2026
intro: Moonshot AI had the biggest day in the feed — a $3.5B funding round, Kimi K3 landing on Microsoft Foundry via Fireworks AI, and an open-sourced RL environment (AgentENV) — cementing its open-weight strategy even as scrutiny over China-linked training data follows it.

Security dominated everything else: a self-replicating prompt-injection worm targeting Word, a joint letter from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, and Meta urging a slower pace of AI development, and fresh defense-in-depth guidance for MCP in production.
highlights: Moonshot AI closed a $3.5B round and pushed Kimi K3 onto Microsoft Foundry via Fireworks AI while open-sourcing AgentENV for agentic RL.
A new prompt-injection variant upgrades attacks against Microsoft Word into full self-replicating worms.
OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, and Meta cosigned a letter urging labs to slow down, alongside reports of a machine-speed cyberattack tied to Hugging Face.
LangChain's Deep Agents v0.7 cuts base input tokens 65% at comparable performance.
AWS and Google Cloud both shipped new agent-platform tooling — Bedrock AgentCore MCP connectors and Gemini Enterprise ADLC automation.
OpenAI's GPT-5.6 optimizes for efficiency per dollar, and ChatGPT opened free access to 100,000 academic researchers.

categories.name: Agent Runtimes & Orchestration
